 403:     def _build_generated_engine(self):
 404:         # Fixed inert construction only; no constructor/module/callback may be
 405:         # supplied by a caller. The real namespace/load-parameters gate is still
 406:         # closed. One owner operation covers checks, construction and commit.
 407:         owner = attempt = None
 408:         try:
 409:             with self._owner_operation("engine"):
 410:                 owner = self.registry
 411:                 attempt = owner._begin_generated_engine(
 412:                     self._permit, self._generated_namespace, self._product)
 413:                 model = _GeneratedEngineModel(attempt.namespace, attempt.product.vad)
 414:                 owner._retain_generated_engine_model(attempt, model)
 415:                 model.prepare()
 416:                 owner._check_generated_engine_model_ready(attempt)
 417:                 pipeline = _GeneratedEnginePipeline(model, attempt.product.vad)
 418:                 owner._retain_generated_engine_pipeline(attempt, pipeline)
 419:                 pipeline.prepare()
 420:                 return owner._publish_generated_engine(attempt)
 421:         except BaseException as original:
 422:             if attempt is not None:
 423:                 try:
 424:                     owner._fail_generated_engine(attempt, original)
 425:                 except BaseException as cleanup:
 426:                     BaseException.add_note(original, "Engine custody update unconfirmed: " + type(cleanup).__name__)
 427:             raise

 457:     @contextmanager
 458:     def use_operation(self):
 459:         # A fixed future dispatcher keeps each native/lazy cursor step inside
 460:         # this scope. The token stays local and conveys no model authority.
 461:         with self._owner_operation("use") as token:
 462:             self.registry.assert_vad_binding(self._product)
 463:             yield token
 464:             self.registry.assert_vad_binding(self._product)

 466:     def encode_generated_text(self, text):
 467:         with self.use_operation() as token:
 468:             # Commit passive output under the same owner state lock as revoke.
 469:             # A frame committed first may reach its caller after a later close;
 470:             # controller lifecycle/publication checks still govern consumption.
 471:             with self.registry._lock:
 472:                 _require(not self._closed, "worker_publication_revoked")
 473:                 self.registry.assert_waveform_binding(self._generated_pcm, sample_rate=16000)
 474:                 value = self.registry.publish_generated_text(token, self._generated_pcm, text)
 475:                 return self._channel.encode("done", {"generated_text": value})

 477:     def release_factory_product(self):
 478:         with self._owner_operation("release"):
 479:             _require(self._factory is not None and self._product is not None, "owned_factory_product_absent")
 480:             # The owner marks the exact VAD inactive, calls the actual factory
 481:             # release, and retains its record if release raises or revoke wins.
 482:             self.registry.retire_vad_product_for_bootstrap(self._permit, self._factory, self._product)
 483:             with self.registry._lock:
 484:                 self.registry._live_locked()
 485:                 _require(not self._closed, "factory_retirement_revoked")
 486:                 self._product = None
 487:                 return {"retired_by_factory": True}

 489:     def accept_initial_control(self, frame):
 490:         """Fixed post-policy begin/cancel entry; consume the raw frame once.
 491: 
 492:         The caller has already completed exact inherited-readset adoption and
 493:         policy acknowledgement. Cancel admits no owner operation or allocation.
 494:         The caller still owns unread-handle release, live-channel closed reply,
 495:         and final revocation. Existing accept_begin remains unchanged.
 496:         """
 497:         try:
 498:             _require(self._ready and not self._started and not self._closed
 499:                      and not self._initial_control_consumed, "initial_control_order")
 500:             operation, payload = self._channel.decode(frame)
 501:             _require((operation == "begin" and payload == {
 502:                          "manifest_sha256": self._channel.binding.manifest_sha256})
 503:                      or (operation == "cancel" and payload == {}), "initial_control_binding")
 504:             self.registry.assert_active()
 505:             self._initial_control_consumed = True
 506:             if operation == "begin":
 507:                 self._started = True
 508:             else:
 509:                 # Also prevent the historical begin entry after consumed cancel.
 510:                 self._ready = False
 511:             return operation
 512:         except BaseException as original:
 513:             self.close_preserving(original)
 514:             raise

 516:     def accept_begin(self, frame):
 517:         _require(self._ready and not self._started and not self._closed, "begin_order")
 518:         try:
 519:             operation, payload = self._channel.decode(frame)
 520:             _require(operation == "begin" and payload == {"manifest_sha256": self._channel.binding.manifest_sha256},
 521:                      "begin_manifest_binding")
 522:             self.registry.assert_active()
 523:             self._started = True
 524:         except BaseException as original:
 525:             self.close_preserving(original)
 526:             raise

 528:     def close_preserving(self, original=None):
 529:         # Retain inputs/factory/product/PCM. This is logical revocation, not a
 530:         # native cancel/join, destructor call or durable recovery observation.
 531:         self._closed = True
 532:         self._ready = False
 533:         self._started = False
 534:         if original is not None:
 535:             self._quarantined = True
 536:         first = original
 537:         failures = []
 538:         # Each revocation is attempted even if the other raises. Preserve the
 539:         # first exception identity; notes never replace the original failure.
 540:         for operation in (self._revoke_owner, self._channel.revoke):
 541:             try:
 542:                 operation()
 543:             except BaseException as error:
 544:                 self._quarantined = True
 545:                 failures.append(type(error).__name__)
 546:                 if first is None:
 547:                     first = error
 548:                 else:
 549:                     BaseException.add_note(first, "Worker revocation remains unconfirmed: " + type(error).__name__)
 550:         if original is None and first is not None:
 551:             raise first

 554:         if self.registry is not None:
 555:             self.registry.revoke_generation(self._permit)

 558: class ControllerHandshake:
 559:     def __init__(self, channel, local_session, local_permit, primitives, native_worker):
 560:         _require(type(channel) is GenerationChannel and channel._send_direction == 0, "controller_channel_required")
 561:         # These references stay in the controller. Fixed lifecycle code must
 562:         # compare the actual record/permit identity and live state at each call.
 563:         self._channel, self._session, self._permit = channel, local_session, local_permit
 564:         self._primitives, self._worker = primitives, native_worker
 565:         self._sent = False
 566:         self._ready = False
 567:         self._begun = False
 568: 
 569:     def _owned_phase(self, startup):
 570:         with self._session._manager._lock:
 571:             record = self._session._record
 572:             _require(self._session._manager._records.get(record.key) is record and record.owner is self._session,
 573:                      "controller_owner_identity")
 574:             _require(record.permit is self._permit and not self._session._revoked and not self._session._closing,
 575:                      "controller_permit_identity")
 576:             _require(record.phase is (Phase.NATIVE_RESERVED if startup else Phase.NATIVE_RUNNING), "controller_phase")
 577:             _require(any(worker is self._worker for worker in self._primitives.workers)
 578:                      and self._worker.read_set is record.protection and self._worker.assigned
 579:                      and not self._worker.unconfirmed and not self._worker.shutdown_started
 580:                      and self._worker.creation_time == self._channel.binding.process_creation_time,
 581:                      "owned_process_generation_binding")
 582: 
 583:     def challenge(self):
 584:         self._owned_phase(True)
 585:         _require(not self._sent, "challenge_single_use")
 586:         self._sent = True
 587:         return self._channel.encode("challenge", {"generation": self._channel.binding.generation_hex,
 588:                                                    "namespace_sha256": self._channel.binding.namespace_sha256})
 589: 
 590:     def accept_ready(self, frame):
 591:         self._owned_phase(True)
 592:         _require(self._sent and not self._ready, "ready_order")
 593:         operation, payload = self._channel.decode(frame)
 594:         _require(operation == "ready" and payload == {"generation": self._channel.binding.generation_hex,
 595:                  "namespace_sha256": self._channel.binding.namespace_sha256}, "worker_ready_binding")
 596:         self._owned_phase(True)
 597:         self._ready = True
 598: 
 599:     def begin(self):
 600:         self._owned_phase(False)
 601:         _require(self._ready and not self._begun, "controller_worker_not_ready_or_already_begun")
 602:         frame = self._channel.encode("begin", {"manifest_sha256": self._channel.binding.manifest_sha256})
 603:         self._begun = True
 604:         return frame
